review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions in ASC134.lean that the two final theorems use (C134NotCentralizer11 and C134NotCentralizer13). The `2 ≤ 2^n` calc also appears in notCentralizerCore_of_natural (hq), but there it is a short calculation about `Nat.card F`, so I did not count it. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemma statements are untested sketches. I inferred that `hidx` in both case structures is an equation `(centerOf (Vq G₀ L) ⊓ centralizer X).relIndex (centerOf (Vq G₀ L)) = 2^n`. I got this from how it is used (`hidx.le`, `rw [hidx]`), not from reading the MS93Case11 and MS93Case13 definitions. findings.problem: Both theorems prove the `hdec` hypothesis of notCentralizerCore_of_natural with the same argument. From `Xq G₀ ≤ Zq G₀ L ⊔ Uq G₀ R L` they get `x ∈ Zq G₀ L ⊔ centerOf (Vq G₀ L)` by `sup_le_sup_left (Uq_le_centerOf_Vq h) _ (hX hx)`. They then turn the join into a product set using `Subgroup.coe_mul_of_left_le_normalizer_right` and the normalizer fact `Zq_le.trans …`. Finally they destructure `x = c * z`. Lines 326–330 repeat this inline, with the normalizer hypothesis supplied as `Zq_le.trans hGZ` in place of the precomputed `hZN`. Case 13 then continues with a second decomposition, so any change to how Xq, Zq and Uq are bounded has to be made in two places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma before the two theorems:
`theorem Xq_mem_mul_centerOf {G₀ R L : Subgroup G} (h : PUHyp G₀ R L) (hX : Xq G₀ ≤ Zq G₀ L ⊔ Uq G₀ R L) (hZN : Zq G₀ L ≤ Subgroup.normalizer (centerOf (Vq G₀ L) : Set G)) : ∀ x ∈ Xq G₀, ∃ c ∈ Zq G₀ L, ∃ z ∈ centerOf (Vq G₀ L), x = c * z`.
Proof sketch: `intro x hx`. Get `hxZ : x ∈ Zq G₀ L ⊔ centerOf (Vq G₀ L)` from `sup_le_sup_left (Uq_le_centerOf_Vq h) _ (hX hx)`. Then `rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, Subgroup.coe_mul_of_left_le_normalizer_right _ _ hZN] at hxZ` and `exact hxZ`. This is the existing code with the final `exact` removed.
Use in case 11: `obtain ⟨c, hc, w, hw, rfl⟩ := Xq_mem_mul_centerOf h hX hZN x hx; exact ⟨c, (Subgroup.mem_inf.mp hc).2, w, hw, rfl⟩`.
Use in case 13: `obtain ⟨c₁, hc₁, z, hz, rfl⟩ := Xq_mem_mul_centerOf h hX (Zq_le.trans hGZ) x hx`, followed by the existing `hz'` step.
Both uses keep their current hypotheses, since `h`, `hX` and the normalizer facts are already in scope.
findings.benefit: The Xq/Zq/centerOf(Vq) decomposition becomes one named, documented fact. Case 11 shrinks to a single `obtain` plus `exact`. Case 13 keeps only its extra Zq-equation step, so the real difference between the cases is visible.

findings.problem: Both theorems prove `¬ centerOf (Vq G₀ L) ≤ centralizer X` with the same argument. Assume the centralizer contains the centre. Then `inf_eq_left` and `relIndex_self` make the relative index 1. This contradicts `hidx : … = 2^n`, because `2 ≤ 2^n` from `hn : 1 ≤ n` (a `calc` via `Nat.pow_le_pow_right`) and `omega` give `1 ≠ 2^n`. The same ten lines occur at 353–360 (`h1'`, `rw [h1'] at hidx`, the `2 ≤ 2 ^ n` calc, `omega`). The `2 ≤ 2^n` calc is also a third time in notCentralizerCore_of_natural (`hq`). Case 13 adds only a preliminary derivation of `hZC`.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma:
`theorem false_of_centerOf_le_centralizer {Z X : Subgroup G} {n : ℕ} (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hidx : (Z ⊓ Subgroup.centralizer (X : Set G)).relIndex Z = 2 ^ n) (hZC : Z ≤ Subgroup.centralizer (X : Set G)) : False`.
Proof sketch: `rw [inf_eq_left.mpr hZC, Subgroup.relIndex_self] at hidx`. Then `have : 2 ≤ 2 ^ n := Nat.le_self_pow (by omega) 2`, or keep the existing calc, and finish with `omega`. This is the existing code, generalised from `centerOf (Vq G₀ L)` to an arbitrary subgroup `Z`.
Use in case 11: `refine ⟨X, hXpar, hidx.le, fun hle => false_of_centerOf_le_centralizer hn hidx hle, hXR⟩`.
Use in case 13: `fun hle => ?_` becomes `false_of_centerOf_le_centralizer hn hidx hZC`, where the `hZC` derivation stays inline.
Both uses supply the same `hn` and `hidx`.
findings.benefit: A ten-line index-counting argument now appears once and is stated as a clear mathematical fact. Each theorem's second bullet drops the duplicated `h1'`/`rw`/`calc`/`omega` block. The `2 ≤ 2^n` fact is then proved in one place for this purpose.
